plugin.name: evidence-ops
plugin.description: Chain-of-custody evidence handling — hash, timestamp, inspect metadata, append to an immutable custody register, package as BagIt, verify, and sync to WORM or S3 Object Lock storage.

skills.name: environment-check
skills.summary: Use when the user wants to know which evidence-handling tools are present on this host before running a pipeline — probes hashing, metadata, timestamping, packaging, and storage CLIs and reports what is missing with an install hint for each

command.name: check
command.description: Probe this host for evidence-handling CLIs and report what is present, missing, and how to install it.
command.body: No arguments. Report a table of tool, status, and install hint, then name the pipeline stages that are currently blocked.

skills.name: install-deps
skills.summary: Use after environment-check reports missing tools — installs them, putting Python-based tools in a plugin-owned virtual environment instead of mutating the system Python

skills.name: init-evidence-store
skills.summary: Use when starting a new evidence collection or adding custody handling to an existing workspace — creates the evidence directory tree, an empty append-only register, and a written record of the hashing policy in force
triggers: set up chain of custody here

command.name: init
command.description: Create the evidence directory tree and an empty append-only custody register in the current workspace.
command.body: The optional target directory arrives in $ARGUMENTS and defaults to the current working directory. Refuse to overwrite an existing register.

skills.name: capture-web
skills.summary: Use when a web page needs to be preserved as evidence — archives it as a single self-contained file, records the capture context that the page itself cannot prove, hashes the result, and offers to register it
triggers: save this page before it changes

command.name: capture
command.description: Archive a URL as a self-contained file, hash it, and record the capture context.
command.body: The URL and any flags arrive in $ARGUMENTS.

skills.name: hash-evidence
skills.summary: Use when a file or directory needs cryptographic hashes — computes SHA-256 by default and optionally BLAKE3, emitting a checkable manifest for directories

command.name: hash
command.description: Compute SHA-256 (and optionally BLAKE3) for a file or directory and write a checkable manifest.
command.body: The path and any flags arrive in $ARGUMENTS.

skills.name: inspect-metadata
skills.summary: Use when the embedded metadata of a file matters — extracts EXIF, IPTC, XMP, and container metadata to JSON, then flags anomalies such as timestamp disagreement or editing-software markers as signals worth investigating
triggers: check this video for editing traces

command.name: metadata
command.description: Extract EXIF, IPTC, XMP, and container metadata to JSON and flag anomalies worth investigating.
command.body: The path and any flags arrive in $ARGUMENTS.

skills.name: log-custody
skills.summary: Use when an item must enter the custody record — hashes it, captures who handed it over and how, copies the original into immutable storage under its own name, and appends one record to the append-only register
triggers: record chain of custody for this file

command.name: log
command.description: Hash an item, capture its custody metadata, and append one record to the append-only evidence register.
command.body: The path and any custody details arrive in $ARGUMENTS. Ask for anything still missing before writing.

skills.name: timestamp-evidence
skills.summary: Use when a file's existence at a point in time needs to be provable independently of the filesystem — anchors its hash with OpenTimestamps and stores the proof alongside the custody record

command.name: timestamp
command.description: Anchor a file's hash with OpenTimestamps, or upgrade and verify an existing proof.
command.body: The path and any flags arrive in $ARGUMENTS.

skills.name: bag-evidence
skills.summary: Use when a set of items must be handed over or archived as one unit — packages a directory as a BagIt bag with per-file checksums and a manifest that any receiving party can validate without this plugin

command.name: bag
command.description: Package a directory as a BagIt bag with per-file checksums and a validatable manifest.
command.body: The source directory and any flags arrive in $ARGUMENTS.

skills.name: verify-bundle
skills.summary: Use when integrity must be confirmed rather than assumed — recomputes every hash, validates bags and timestamp proofs, and reports an explicit pass or fail naming each diverging file
triggers: check the bag is still valid

command.name: verify
command.description: Recompute hashes, validate bags and timestamp proofs, and report an explicit pass or fail.
command.body: The path arrives in $ARGUMENTS and defaults to the current working directory.

skills.name: setup-storage
skills.summary: Use when configuring where evidence is replicated — walks through defining a storage remote, confirms its retention or write-once behaviour, and records the destination policy without ever touching credentials
triggers: where should evidence be backed up

skills.name: sync-immutable
skills.summary: Use when verified evidence should be replicated to storage that cannot silently rewrite it — copies to the configured remote, confirms retention settings before writing, and re-verifies what landed

command.name: sync
command.description: Replicate verified evidence to immutable storage and re-verify what landed.
command.body: The path and any flags arrive in $ARGUMENTS. Always dry-run first unless told otherwise.

skills.name: reference-lookup
skills.summary: Use when deciding how to handle a media type, storage mode, or integrity question — searches this plugin's own reference corpus and returns the most relevant passages with their file paths
triggers: what is object lock compliance mode

command.name: lookup
command.description: Search this plugin's reference corpus and return the most relevant passages with their paths.

skills.name: onboard
skills.summary: Use on first run or on a new machine — checks the environment, offers to install what is missing, configures a storage destination, and ends by showing the shortest working pipeline for this host
triggers: get me started with evidence handling

command.name: onboard
command.description: First-run setup — environment check, dependency install, and storage configuration.
command.body: No arguments. Run the stages in order and stop at the first one the user declines.
